sentences.text: Heard Sri Shivasai M.Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y.Devareddiyavara, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.

2. The petitioner herein is seeking regular bail in Crime No.94/2022 for the offence u/sec.341, 212,
376(2)(L), 376-D r/w 34 of IPC.
3. Sri Mohan Shivappa Balambida has lodged a complaint stating that he is having four children.
The second child is a victim in this case.
The victim is aged about 18 years one month as on the date of alleged incident.
The victim is handicapped by birth.
4. On 31.05.2022 at about 4.15 p.m., when the victim was sitting in front of her house, the accused Nos.1 and 2 took her inside the house and committed rape.
CW.9 being a younger sister of the victim after finishing her school came back to house.
The front door was locked from inside.
CW.9 calling the name of the victim by knocking the door after sometime, she has heard the noise of opening the door.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13202 CW.9 after having seen the person inside the house raised alarm and made the localities to assemble in front of her house.
The people of the locality came and enquired about the incident and also name of the accused.
The accused have disclosed their identity and escaped from the clutches of the mob.

5. The complainant has lodged a complaint before the respondent police, the respondent police have registered a case in Crime No.94/2022 for the offences stated supra and after conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
6. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.2.

The allegations made against the petitioner is that he has committed rape along with accused No.1 on the victim and also trying to harbored the accused No.1.
7.
It is further submitted that the petitioner has not been identified by the victim and his name has not been mentioned in the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

The petitioner is the earning member of the family and he will abide by the conditions imposed by the Court in the NC:
2023:KHC-D:13202 event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

2 8.

entities.text: Shantappa Benageri Alias ... vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the petitioner herein has committed heinous offence against the handicapped girl.

The statement recorded u/sec.164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim, the victim has stated the name of the petitioner herein and also explained the agony which she has undergone at the instance of the petitioner and another.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.

Making such submission,
the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet and also the statement of the victim, it makes it clear that the petitioner and another have committed rape on the physically handicapped girl.
The petitioner and another have been identified by CW9 and also the people of the locality have caught hold the petitioner and another red-handedly.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:13202 Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is rejected.

Sd/-
JUDGE CLK Yashavant S/O
